steps: Follow the Installation steps above to install Core and enable it with your other HoloSuite modules.
Reload the world after changing modules so every app can register with Core.
Open HoloSuite from its scene-control button, the configured keybinding, the module settings menu, or a macro that calls game.holosuite.openLauncher().
Choose Apps and select a tile. GMs see every registered app; players see only apps that explicitly allow player access.
Open Settings inside the launcher to pick the device style. Use Foundry Module Settings for world-wide theme, player-access, and debugging options.

callouts.title: Core is a launcher, not a data store
callouts.text: Contacts, cases, maps, terminals, and other feature data remain owned by their respective modules. Disabling Core removes the common launcher but does not erase that module data.

steps: Open Galactic Records from HoloSuite Core.
Drag an Actor, Token, or Actor folder onto New Record. If you are viewing People, Vessels, or Organizations, new records use that type automatically.
Open a record and use Edit section to add the details you want. Save each section when you are done.
Drag other records into Associates or Assets to link them. You can also drag a Scene into Last Seen.
Open the cog inside Galactic Records to choose what appears on cards and whether wanted levels appear over tokens.
If players should use the database, enable Allow players to search records in Foundry's module settings. They only receive information their user is allowed to see.
Enable HoloSuite Core and CyberCall, then open CyberCall from the launcher.
As GM, open the call composer and choose a caller name, subtitle or faction, portrait, message, signal strength, visual variant, ringtone, and recipients.
Use Preview Locally to check the presentation without contacting anyone.
Choose Broadcast to Players. Recipients receive the ringing or incoming-call display; the synchronized call opens when accepted.
Use Close Active Call to end the current call on connected clients.
Draw a Region on the source Scene if you want a cropped live feed. Static-image cameras do not need a Region.
Open Security Cameras from HoloSuite and select New.
Enter a name and location, choose Live Scene or Static Image, select the Scene/Region or image, then choose a status and display mode.
Save the camera and use Preview to check it on the GM client.
Choose Show to Players to broadcast it. Use Close Feeds when the scene should end.
Open CSI Toolkit as GM and choose New Case.
Set the title, subtitle, status, board theme, image, and description, then save.
Open Board and right-click empty space to add Evidence, Suspect, Location, or Timeline cards.
Right-click or use the connection action to connect two cards, then choose a label, relationship type, line style, and color.
Drag cards into position and select Publish Layout so collaborators receive the saved arrangement.
Open Galaxy Map from HoloSuite as GM and choose Create Map.
Edit the map title, subtitle, description, background image, and visibility.
Create at least two systems, position them on the map, and mark them player-visible.
Create a route between the systems and mark the route player-visible.
Set the party’s current system, then choose Show to broadcast the map to players.
Have a player select the connected destination and Request Travel; all active voters must accept before the current system moves.
Open Bounty Board from HoloSuite as GM and choose New Contract.
Enter a contract ID, title, target, reward, currency, threat, and the public description.
Optionally add faction, location, comma-separated tags, image, long dossier text, linked Journal, and claimed-by text.
Enable Published to Players and save, or save privately and use Publish from the card.
Ask a player to open the board, filter or search, expand the card, and choose Request Contract.
Use Assign to mark it Claimed, then Complete or Mark Failed when the job resolves.
Enable HoloSuite Core and Critical Cut-In, then open Configure Player Cut-Ins.
Choose the check die and whether high or low rolls are positive. Confirming a change resets every listed threshold to the new die’s best/worst endpoints; Save applies it.
Set global success and failure thresholds, duration, and each Actor’s Success and Failure tabs.
For each desired cut-in, enable it and choose art, audio, threshold override, animation, overlay text, and accent color.
Roll the selected die in a non-damage roll and verify the natural result qualifies.
Open HoloSuite Hacking as GM and choose a minigame, player, and owned hacker Actor.
For Full Setup, choose a detected skill, roll source, roll rules, DC, and live audience. For Quick Hack, choose a fixed outcome instead.
Use Test Yourself to preview locally, or Send to Player for a live challenge.
The player accepts. Native modes open the system roll, Sheet mode waits for a new chat roll, and Custom mode rolls the configured dice.
The resulting profile generates the puzzle. Spectators can watch but cannot interact.
The puzzle’s actual completion is reported to the GM and any registered integration callback.

callouts.title: Roll outcome is difficulty, not final success
callouts.text: Even Critical Failure launches a playable puzzle, and even Critical Success still requires the player to solve it.

paragraphs: Start with one ship and one piece of equipment.
steps: Follow the Installation steps above, then open your world as a GM.
Open the HoloSuite launcher and select HoloDock. Players also open HoloDock from this launcher.
As GM, select the plus button beside Ship Profile. HoloDock creates New Ship with a default image, sample statistics, and four empty slots.
Expand Ship Setup. Enter the ship name and class, choose an image, set Power Capacity, and select Save Ship. Use 0 when you do not want a total power budget.

Open a Foundry Item that represents a ship system. Select the rocket-shaped Ship Equipment control in the Item sheet header, enable Ship Equipment, choose its category, and configure any activation, durability, or power options.
Drag the Item from its sheet or directory onto a compatible empty slot in HoloDock. Confirm the install. You can also open a slot's three-dot menu and select Choose to browse world Items.
Select the installed Item in the right-hand Equipment rail to inspect it, allocate power, change durability, open its Item sheet, remove it from the slot, or activate it.
Open Player Rights from the shield button beside the profile selector. Decide whether players can see the ship, request installs, and activate systems.

callouts.title: Recommended first test
callouts.text: Create one powered Item with Power Draw 2 and Starting Allocation 2, give the ship Power Capacity 5, and enable activation. This makes the Systems, Power Grid, and activation views useful immediately.

steps: Draw one or more Foundry Regions where the machine should be accessible.
Open Module Settings and choose the currency source, fallback label/item, optional Actor path, player launcher access, and audio.
Open Vending Machines → Create. Name and style it, choose Online, link Regions, and leave Require presence enabled for physical access.
Drop Items from the world, a compendium, or an Actor sheet into the inventory; set display art, description, price, stock, and maximum for up to six products.
Save & Test with a controlled/assigned Actor, then enter the linked Region as a player and make a small purchase.
Verify the success entry in Recent Transactions.

paragraphs: Start with an existing Scene, add rooms and markers, then check what players will see.
steps: Follow the Installation steps above, then activate a Scene that contains Foundry walls.
Open the HoloSuite launcher and select Blueprint, or use Open Blueprint in Scene Controls.
Open Settings. Enter a Location name and optional Facility designation, keep Generated from Scene selected, choose a theme, and save.
Open Rooms and select Auto-detect Rooms. Review the number of closed spaces found, accept them, then edit the generated room names and optional details.
Use Marker to place an entrance, objective, hazard, terminal, or another icon. Use Text for a plain label and Pencil for a temporary route or note.
Switch from GM View to Player View. Check the hidden-information badge and verify that GM-only details and unrevealed secret doors do not appear.
Select Present to Players to open the filtered blueprint for connected players. Use Export PNG when you also want a static handout.
If a HoloSuite Terminal should keep the plan available, return to Settings and select Publish Layout, then link the published layout from that Terminal profile's Layout app.

callouts.title: Start with clean wall data
callouts.text: Generated architecture and automatic rooms follow the Scene's walls. Gaps, overlapping endpoints, and decorative wall fragments can create unexpected outlines or prevent a room from closing.

steps: Enable HoloSuite Core and Terminal. Enable HoloSuite Hacking and Security Cameras too if this terminal needs those integrations.
Open Terminal Manager from HoloSuite or Module Settings and create a Terminal Profile.
Set its name, theme, desktop style, enabled apps, and current-scene Regions.
Create or attach a mail account and file folder, then add at least one message and one file.
Set player access levels/overrides and optional password or hacking authentication.
Save, enter a linked Region with a player-owned token, and verify boot, login, apps, and content from a player client.

callouts.title: Integrations are optional
callouts.text: Terminal itself works without HoloSuite Hacking or Security Cameras. Hacking buttons and camera feeds require those modules; disabling an integration preserves saved Terminal configuration.

paragraphs: Pulse Scanner is system-agnostic and supports Foundry VTT v12–v14. HoloSuite Core is required. Use the updated Core build for the launcher’s Create hotbar macro option.
steps: On the active scene, use Foundry’s Region tools to draw an area around a secret door, clue, object, or other scan target.
Open Pulse Scanner as GM. On Targets, click Add target, choose What is it?, select the region under Where is it?, and enter a name. The type suggests a signal, marker, and color. Click Create target.

On Scanners, expand Give scanner at the top. Choose a player character, a matching signal, and the range in scene units. The list includes characters owned by a player or assigned to a player’s user account.
Leave the scanner unlimited, or enable Limited charges and set its capacity. Expand Name and appearance to rename it or choose a pulse animation, then click Give scanner.

Select one token on the map and click Preview beside an assigned scanner to try it. You can also preview the settings in Give scanner before assigning it. Previews stay local, use no charges, and keep the manager open.
As a player, select an owned token, open Pulse Scanner, and choose a scanner from the wheel. A scan spends one charge when charges are limited and highlights matching areas within range.

callouts.title: Match the signal
callouts.text: A Structural scanner detects Structural targets. The target form warns when no assigned scanner uses the target’s signal. Enable player scanning in the module settings if players cannot scan.

sections.title: Managing targets
paragraphs: The Targets tab keeps the essentials visible: type, region, and name. Search by name, region, or signal, and filter active or resolved targets. Move the manager with the top-middle grip; the integrated Close button is at the top right.

Expand Detection and player notes to change the signal, note visibility, or notes. Expand Appearance and advanced options for the map marker, color, and integrity on breakable targets. Changes apply when you save.
Choose Scanner Reticle, Type Icon, Region Outline, or Scent Cloud for the map marker. Scent targets default to a softly drifting cloud clipped to the detected area.

Use Preview on map to try the target with player label settings. For a region with multiple areas, select exactly one token first. The preview uses its matching scanner range, or the default scanner range when it has none. Single-area targets can be previewed without selecting a token.

Right-click a target in the list and choose Delete to remove it immediately. Under Target actions, Mark resolved excludes it from future scans; Enable scanning again restores detection. These actions apply to the saved target without changing its note visibility.

sections.title: One target, multiple areas
paragraphs: One target can link to one Scene Region containing several separate shapes. For three secret doors, draw three rectangles in the same region and create one Hidden Passage target linked to that region.

Each area is checked separately against scan range. Only reached areas receive pings, labels, outlines, or scent effects. Empty space between distant shapes does not trigger detection. Scanner previews use the same detection rules.

All areas share the target’s name, signal, notes, appearance, integrity, and resolved state. Use separate targets and regions when doors need independent states. Existing links work without migration; duplicate targets on the same region are not automatically removed.

sections.title: Scanners and pulse animations
paragraphs: Assigned scanners are grouped by character. Use Edit scanner to change the name, signal, range, charges, or pulse animation. Recharge refills a limited scanner. New limited scanners start fully charged; unlimited scanners need no recharge.
Choose from five pulse animations: Classic Radar, Echo Rings, Sonar Sweep, Grid Burst, and Glitch Pulse. Animation changes the scan’s appearance; the signal and range determine what it detects.
Scanner access belongs to the character’s actor, so there is no scanner Item to create or equip. A character can have multiple scanners with different signals and settings.

sections.title: Player controls and recharge
paragraphs: Hover or focus a scanner on the wheel to inspect its name, signal, range, animation, and charges. Click it to scan. Opening the wheel alone does not spend charges. A character with one scanner gets a compact layout.

Arrow keys cycle through scanners. Enter or Space activates the selected scanner; number keys select and activate matching wheel positions. Click outside, right-click, or press Escape to close the wheel.

Empty scanners can be selected but cannot scan. Use Recharge in the center to refill the selected scanner. A successful recharge posts a chat message naming the character and scanner. Full scanners show Fully charged; unlimited scanners have no recharge button.

Players can scan only from tokens they own. If no token is selected, opening Pulse Scanner uses the assigned character’s token only when exactly one is on the current scene. If the choice is ambiguous, select a token explicitly.

sections.title: Shortcut and hotbar macro
steps: In Foundry’s Configure Controls > Pulse Scanner, bind Open Pulse Scanner to your preferred key. The shortcut is unassigned by default. It opens the wheel for players and the manager for GMs.
Right-click Pulse Scanner in the HoloSuite launcher and choose Create hotbar macro. You can also focus the launcher button and press Shift+F10 to open its menu.
The macro sheet opens. Drag the macro from Foundry’s Macros directory onto your hotbar. Repeating Create hotbar macro reuses your generated macro instead of creating duplicates.
paragraphs: Players need Foundry’s Create Macros and Use Script Macros permissions for the macro option. The shortcut and macro follow the same token-selection and player-scanning rules as the launcher.
Existing script macros can call: await game.pulseScanner.openScanner();

sections.title: Scanner signals
bullets: Structural: walls, supports, hidden passages, and weak construction.
Arcane: magical signatures, wards, enchantments, and ley traces.
Thermal: heat sources, engines, and recent activity.
Forensic: residue, fingerprints, evidence, and traces.
Tech: devices, transmitters, and electronic signatures.
Biological: organic matter, toxins, parasites, and living organisms.
Scent: lingering odors, spoor, chemical traces, and trails.
paragraphs: The target’s Detected by setting determines which signal finds it. Nearby token outlines are controlled separately and can appear in every signal mode.

sections.title: Player visibility and settings
paragraphs: Player notes set to Hidden are omitted from player scan results. Names follow the world’s player-label setting independently of note visibility. Shown notes appear when player labels are enabled. Hiding notes does not prevent detection.
In Configure Settings > Pulse Scanner, adjust player scan permissions, label and integrity visibility, highlight duration, and scan sound. Integrity bars apply to breakable targets when enabled.
Target data is stored on the scene for module operation. Hidden notes are a presentation control, not secure storage against users inspecting client-side scene data.

sections.title: Token detection
paragraphs: Scans can outline other tokens in range without regions or target setup. The scanning token is excluded. In Configure Settings > Pulse Scanner > Token Detection, choose one of the following modes.
bullets: Visible tokens: the default; respects each viewer’s token visibility.
Through walls — non-hidden tokens: includes tokens outside the viewer’s vision, but excludes hidden GM tokens for players.
Off — region targets only: disables token outlines.

callouts.title: Temporary outlines
callouts.text: Outlines follow the token artwork, move with the token, and fade automatically. They do not change token visibility or reveal actor data. Opaque portraits outline their image boundary; video or unavailable artwork uses a rectangular fallback.

sections.title: Advanced notes
paragraphs: Reveal, hide, import, and export helpers remain available through game.pulseScanner. The scan API returns one result per detected target, with transient scanAreas for the reached areas. Those contacts are not saved as additional targets.

The local pulse-scanner.scanComplete hook supplies sceneId, userId, and anonymous x/y points for detected region areas. It includes no target names, notes, or actor references. Token contacts are not included. Empty successful scans emit an empty points list; denied scans do not emit.
Rendering is limited to 80 region contacts and up to 80 token contacts per pulse. Up to 12 detected scent areas render as clouds; additional scent hits fall back to outlines.
